name: stalwart-mail-mcp

tools.name: mail_list_mailboxes
tools.description:
Returns the available accounts (your mailbox plus shared ones), folders with message counts (unread) and the addresses you can send from.
Call it first when you do not know which folders or accounts exist. Changes nothing.

account.description: Which account: leave empty for the signed-in mailbox, or name a shared mailbox / group you have access to (the part before @ is enough; a full address works too). mail_list_mailboxes shows what exists.

tools.name: mail_search_emails
tools.description:
Searches mail (full text, sender, recipient, subject, folder, date, unread, attachments) or lists a whole thread.
Returns message ids (for mail_get_email), thread, sender, date and a preview. Newest first, paging through limit/offset.
Without a filter it returns the latest messages from all folders (trash included) — for “what is new” use mailbox="inbox", unread=true.

account.description: Which account: leave empty for the signed-in mailbox, or name a shared mailbox / group you have access to (the part before @ is enough; a full address works too). mail_list_mailboxes shows what exists.

text.description: Full text across subject, body and headers.

from.description: Sender (part of the name or address).

to.description: Recipient (part of the name or address).

mailbox.description: Folder: inbox, sent, drafts, trash, junk, archive, or a folder name.

after.description: Only messages received from this date on (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO 8601).

before.description: Only messages received up to this date (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO 8601).

has_attachment.description: true = only messages with an attachment.

thread_id.description: List every message of this thread (threadId from an earlier result); other filters are then ignored.

tools.name: mail_get_email
tools.description:
Returns a whole message by id (from mail_search_emails): headers, body text (HTML is converted to text) and the list of attachments.
mail_get_attachment reads an attachment's content (PDF, image, text). To reply use mail_send_email with in_reply_to_id. Changes nothing (does not mark the message as read).

account.description: Which account: leave empty for the signed-in mailbox, or name a shared mailbox / group you have access to (the part before @ is enough; a full address works too). mail_list_mailboxes shows what exists.

html.description: true = return the original HTML instead of converted text.

tools.name: mail_get_attachment
tools.description:
Downloads an attachment of a received message, saves it to disk and returns its content: text for text files, the text of every page for PDFs, the picture for images.
Scans (PDF pages without a text layer) and photos of documents are read through OCR, tables included; pages that came from OCR are marked “(OCR)” — treat numbers from them with some caution and ask for a preview when a figure matters.
Other types (docx, xlsx, zip…) only return the path of the saved file.
Pick the attachment by name or by its number from the list in mail_get_email; a message with a single attachment needs neither. The message itself is not changed.

account.description: Which account: leave empty for the signed-in mailbox, or name a shared mailbox / group you have access to (the part before @ is enough; a full address works too). mail_list_mailboxes shows what exists.

attachment.description: Attachment name (a part is enough, e.g. “invoice”) or its number starting at 1.

page_to.description: PDF: last page to return (default: the last one).

preview.description: PDF: also attach an image of page 1 (chart, stamp, signature, checking the OCR).

ocr.description: false = do not send scans and photos to the OCR provider, return the image only.

save_dir.description: Folder to save the file to; default /tmp/Downloads/Mail-Attachments.

tools.name: mail_send_email
tools.description:
Sends an e-mail from the mailbox — a new one, or a reply (in_reply_to_id). A copy is stored in Sent.
It sends IMMEDIATELY and cannot be undone. Send only when the user explicitly said the message should go out; otherwise create a draft (mail_create_draft).
Verify the recipient before sending — never guess an unknown address, look it up with mail_search_contacts.

account.description: Which account: leave empty for the signed-in mailbox, or name a shared mailbox / group you have access to (the part before @ is enough; a full address works too). mail_list_mailboxes shows what exists.

from.description: Sender address; default is the address of the signed-in mailbox. Must be one of the account's allowed senders.

to.description: Recipients — a list of addresses as “name@domain” or “First Last <name@domain>”.

cc.description: Cc — a list of addresses as “name@domain” or “First Last <name@domain>”.

bcc.description: Bcc — a list of addresses as “name@domain” or “First Last <name@domain>”.

reply_to.description: Reply-To (where replies should go) — a list of addresses as “name@domain” or “First Last <name@domain>”.

subject.description: Subject. A reply gets “Re: …” automatically when it is missing.

text.description: Message body as plain text (preferred). Write the signature yourself, the server adds none.

html.description: Body as HTML (optional; when text is missing it is derived from the HTML).

in_reply_to_id.description: id of the message you are replying to — sets the thread (In-Reply-To/References), fills in the recipient and subject, marks the original as answered.

reply_all.description: For a reply: also copy the other original recipients.

attachments.description: Full paths of files on this computer to attach (max. 25 MB each).

tools.name: mail_create_draft
tools.description: Saves a message as a draft in the Drafts folder (does not send). The user can then review it in webmail or on the phone and send it themselves, or mail_send_draft sends it by id. Same parameters as mail_send_email (including replying via in_reply_to_id and attachments).

account.description: Which account: leave empty for the signed-in mailbox, or name a shared mailbox / group you have access to (the part before @ is enough; a full address works too). mail_list_mailboxes shows what exists.

from.description: Sender address; default is the address of the signed-in mailbox. Must be one of the account's allowed senders.

to.description: Recipients — a list of addresses as “name@domain” or “First Last <name@domain>”.

cc.description: Cc — a list of addresses as “name@domain” or “First Last <name@domain>”.

bcc.description: Bcc — a list of addresses as “name@domain” or “First Last <name@domain>”.

reply_to.description: Reply-To (where replies should go) — a list of addresses as “name@domain” or “First Last <name@domain>”.

subject.description: Subject. A reply gets “Re: …” automatically when it is missing.

text.description: Message body as plain text (preferred). Write the signature yourself, the server adds none.

html.description: Body as HTML (optional; when text is missing it is derived from the HTML).

in_reply_to_id.description: id of the message you are replying to — sets the thread (In-Reply-To/References), fills in the recipient and subject, marks the original as answered.

reply_all.description: For a reply: also copy the other original recipients.

attachments.description: Full paths of files on this computer to attach (max. 25 MB each).

tools.name: mail_send_draft
tools.description: Sends an existing draft by id (from mail_create_draft or from a search in the drafts folder). Sends immediately — only on the user's explicit instruction.

account.description: Which account: leave empty for the signed-in mailbox, or name a shared mailbox / group you have access to (the part before @ is enough; a full address works too). mail_list_mailboxes shows what exists.

from.description: Sending address, when it differs from the draft's From header.

tools.name: mail_delete_draft
tools.description: Permanently deletes a draft by id. Works only on messages flagged as drafts — it never deletes sent or received mail.

account.description: Which account: leave empty for the signed-in mailbox, or name a shared mailbox / group you have access to (the part before @ is enough; a full address works too). mail_list_mailboxes shows what exists.

tools.name: mail_search_contacts
tools.description:
Finds an e-mail address or phone number: searches the address books (your own and shared ones) and also the mail history (who wrote to you and whom you wrote to, matching the query).
Use it whenever you need a person's or company's address before sending anything. Without a query it lists the whole address book.

query.description: Name, part of an address, company…

account.description: Limit to the address books of one account; default = all.

include_history.description: Also search senders/recipients of mail (only with a query).

limit.description: Max. contacts from the address book per account.

tools.name: mail_add_contact
tools.description:
Creates a contact in an address book. Default is the signed-in mailbox's own address book; pass the account of a shared mailbox to store it in the shared one (everyone with access sees it, on phones too through CardDAV).
Check mail_search_contacts first so you do not create a duplicate.

account.description: Which account: leave empty for the signed-in mailbox, or name a shared mailbox / group you have access to (the part before @ is enough; a full address works too). mail_list_mailboxes shows what exists.

address_book.description: Address book name (default = the account's default address book).

full_name.description: Full name, when splitting it makes no sense (e.g. a company as a contact).
